feedback.end: Air is a gas. Sounds travel most slowly through gases. When a sound is made, it must often travel through both air and another medium to reach our ears.

atoms.a: Which state of matter is air?

instruction.text: Most sounds have to travel through air to reach our ears. Sort the journey of the sound into the correct order.

atoms.text: Then, the vibrations travel through the air.
Finally, the vibrations reach Arnold’s ears.

feedback.end: Space is a vacuum. This means that there is no air and no medium for sound to travel through. This is why astronauts have to talk using radios in their space suits.

atoms.a: In which place is there not any air?

instruction.text: Select the boy who will hear the cat meow sooner.

feedback.end: That’s right! The boy in the blue t-shirt is closer, so the vibrations will reach him before the other boy.

instruction.text: Select the swimmer who will hear the crab snap his claws sooner.

feedback.end: Although both swimmers are similar distances away from the source of the sound, the diver is underwater with the crab. This means that the vibrations only have to travel through one medium to reach their ears.

instruction.text: Select the animal that will hear the wolf howl louder.

feedback.end: Since the squirrel is closer, the vibrations will be stronger when they reach its ears. Sounds get quieter further away from their sources.
